Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

contrast noun

a striking difference between things set side by side

also in contrast, by contrast, contrast with, in contrast to

classical

Cic. Off. 1.57: sī contentiō quaedam et comparātiō fīat (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Pis. 51: fortūnārum (Lewis & Short)

contentiō, contentiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a comparison, a contrast

Setting one thing against another, in thought or in words; in rhetoric, antithesis (Lewis & Short). Not the plain word: its first senses are straining, effort and dispute. Most often Latin shows a contrast by setting two clauses side by side (see whereas) or by comparing (see compare); for the unlikeness itself see difference (dissimilitūdō).

Other words

  • contrā — by contrast, on the other hand

    adverb · also used · classical · Pac. ap. Auct. Her. 2.36: sunt autem aliī philosophī, quī contrā Fortūnam negant ūllam exstāre (Lewis & Short) · Wiktionary

    Lewis & Short: “on the contrary, on the other hand, vice versā; sometimes almost = sed or autem”. As a preposition with the accusative, against, opposite.

Examples

  • sī contentiō quaedam et comparātiō fīat

    if a contrast and comparison of some kind were madeCic. Off. 1.57 (Lewis & Short)

  • fortūnam īnsānam esse … perhibent philosophī … sunt autem aliī philosophī, quī contrā Fortūnam negant ūllam exstāre

    philosophers say that fortune is mad … but there are other philosophers who, by contrast, deny that there is any such thing as FortunePac. ap. Auct. Her. 2.36 (Lewis & Short)

See also compare, difference, whereas, opposite.

SourcesLewis & Short: contentio · Lewis & Short: contra
